findings.reason: s41 lands before s42 and cannot clear this file (it is not in s41's write paths), so s41's gate carries an added failure it is fenced out of repairing unless the rewrite of this one file is moved into s41's write paths or the dependency is declared the other way.
findings.text: s42 is declared to depend on s41 and its write paths carry `tests/test_a_section_reviewed_as_authored_stays_reviewed.py`, but the failure in that file is introduced by s41 alone: its `_review` helper writes the delivered report `RUBRIC wiring: pass` under the design rubric (`_subject` sets `"rubric": "design"`, tests/test_a_section_reviewed_as_authored_stays_reviewed.py:56-61, 81), and `wiring` is not in `PLAN_DESIGN_REVIEW_ITEMS` (reckon/crew/review.py:254-260), so under s41's parse-based admission the parse holds no rubric item and no finding and the report is refused as not-a-review (s41's own done-when case 4 names this rule); the report has no FINDING line, unlike the other two files, whose reports carry `FINDING reuse_search …` / `RUBRIC reuse_search: pass`, both inside the design rubric and therefore admitted

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_delivered_status` sits at reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2118 (cited "near 2118"), `newest_design_review` is read in the gate at reckon/crew/routing.py:2554 (cited "near 2554"), the answer verb's `read_plan_review` is at reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:2555 and its `newest_design_review` call at :2567, and `_review_is_incomplete` is at reckon/crew/plan_review.py:810 (cited "near 811"); all three named test files exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s42's cases are measurable and the node declares a negative control ("restore the rubric test in `_delivered_status`, and the first case stores `ready` and the dispatch is admitted") that I confirmed fails to hold once the narrow rubric test is restored, since `_review_is_incomplete` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:810) is what `review_coverage` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:864) skips on.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate writes under the run's own directory (as s40 states for the same gate) and the two arms are recorded as `baseline_suite`/`after_suite` with `failure_ids`; no node-local or scratchpad path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s42 introduces no new symbol and carries no ticket number, version tag or changelog prose into code; the terms it names (`INCOMPLETE_STATUS`, `_review_is_incomplete`, `PLAN_DESIGN_REVIEW_ITEMS`) are existing mechanism names.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the evidence (`_delivered_status` at plan_review.py:2118 does gate on `plan_report_rubric_name(rubric) == "plan_review"`, and `newest_design_review` at plan_review.py:1220 does not filter `_review_is_incomplete`, so it does offer a partial design review to the gate); the mechanism produces the done-when (removing the rubric test makes `absent_items` the only test, and the gate's refusal naming the design-review command comes from the design branch at routing.py:2560-2571); and both callers are named (`require_plan_reviewed` at routing.py:2554 and `crew review --answer` at crew_dispatch_commands.py:2567, where `read_plan_review` at :2555 resolves through `review_coverage` at plan_review.py:1037 and so skips an incomplete record, refusing at :2563 before `newest_design_review` is consulted — exactly as the section states).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the mark at delivery and the gate's refusal are one verdict (a partial design review covers nothing), and the answer-verb fallback keeps that same review's findings answerable; each half carries its own assertion.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — s42 depends on s41 and repairs a test file that s41 alone reddens, so s41's gate cannot be green (see FINDING wiring).
